steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy, then beat in eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together; add to the batter alternately with milk until just combined.
Divide batter between pans and bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat frosting butter, cocoa, powdered sugar, and milk together until fluffy, then frost between layers and over the top.

filling.note: The chocolate frosting is spread between the layers as well as over the top, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Buttercream
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the frosting butter, cocoa, powdered sugar, and milk together until fluffy.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Frost between the layers and over the top.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and generously grease a 10-cup bundt pan.
Cream butter and sugar, then beat in eggs one at a time until smooth.
Fold in flour and cocoa powder until just combined, then stir in walnuts.
Pour into the bundt pan and bake 50-60 minutes — the center should look slightly underdone. Do not overbake or the tunnel disappears.
Cool in the pan 1-2 hours, invert onto a plate, then drizzle with a milk-thinned powdered sugar glaze.

filling.note: A single bundt cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Milk Glaze
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the powdered sugar with the milk until smooth and pourable.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Drizzle over the cooled, inverted cake.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch round pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt together.
Stir in oil and eggs until just combined, then fold in banana, pineapple, and pecans — do not overmix.
Divide between pans and bake 25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and frost between layers and over the top; garnish with extra pecans.

filling.note: The cream cheese frosting is spread between the layers as well as over the top, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together until smooth and fluffy.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread between the three layers and over the top and sides; garnish with extra chopped pecans.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — cream cheese frosting is not shelf-stable at room temperature.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 9-inch round pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cinnamon, baking soda, and salt together.
Stir in oil and eggs, then fold in carrots, pineapple, and walnuts.
Divide between pans and bake 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and frost between layers and over the top.

filling.note: The cream cheese frosting is spread between the layers as well as over the top, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together until smooth and fluffy.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread between the layers and over the top and sides.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — cream cheese frosting is not shelf-stable at room temperature.

steps: Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F) and butter four ramekins, dusting with cocoa powder.
Melt chocolate and butter together until smooth.
Whisk eggs, egg yolks, and sugar until pale and thick, then fold in the melted chocolate.
Fold in flour and salt just until combined, then divide among the ramekins.
Bake 10-12 minutes until the edges are set but the center still jiggles. Unmold immediately and serve.
storage: Best served immediately; unbaked batter can be refrigerated in the ramekins up to 1 day ahead.

filling.note: A single-batter individual dessert with a molten center that forms during baking — there is no separate filling to add.

frostingFinish.note: Served straight from the ramekin with no applied frosting or glaze.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Whisk flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt together.
In a separate bowl, whisk oil, buttermilk, egg, food coloring, and vinegar, then combine with the dry ingredients.
Divide batter among liners and bake 18-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together and pipe onto the cooled cupcakes.

filling.note: No separate filling is used — these are single-layer cupcakes.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese, butter, and powdered sugar together until smooth.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pipe onto the cooled cupcakes just before serving.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — cream cheese frosting is not shelf-stable at room temperature.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease four 6-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs and vanilla, then alternate adding the flour/baking powder mix with milk.
Divide batter evenly and tint each portion a different color, then pour into pans and bake 22-25 minutes.
Cool completely, then stack and crumb-coat the layers with vanilla buttercream, chilling between coats.
Warm the cream and pour over the white chocolate to make ganache; once slightly cooled, drip it down the sides of the chilled cake.

filling.note: The vanilla buttercream is spread between the layers as a crumb coat, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Vanilla Buttercream & Ganache Drip
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the buttercream butter and powdered sugar together until smooth. Separately, warm the cream and pour over the white chocolate, stirring until glossy.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Crumb-coat and frost the stacked, chilled layers with buttercream first, chilling again. Once the ganache has cooled slightly, drip it down the sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill between the crumb coat and final coat, and again before adding the drip, so it holds a clean edge.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 230°C (450°F) and line a 9-inch springform pan with overlapping parchment that extends well above the rim.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth, then add eggs one at a time.
Mix in heavy cream, salt, and flour until just combined — do not overmix.
Pour into the pan and bake 50-55 minutes until deeply browned on top and the center still wobbles.
Cool at room temperature, then chill at least 4 hours before releasing from the pan.

filling.note: A single baked custard with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: The deeply browned top comes from the high oven heat during baking, not from an applied frosting or glaze.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together.
Beat eggs and sugar until pale and doubled in volume, mix in melted butter and vanilla, then fold in the dry ingredients.
Pour into the pan and bake 25 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely, then poke holes all over the top.
Whisk whole milk, evaporated milk, and condensed milk together and pour slowly over the cake, letting it soak in.
Chill at least 2 hours, then top with whipped cream just before serving.

filling.name: Three-Milk Soak
filling.prep: Whisk the whole milk, evaporated milk, and condensed milk together.
filling.applicationNotes: Poke holes all over the cooled cake, then pour the milk mixture slowly over the top so it soaks all the way through.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill at least 2 hours so the soak fully absorbs before serving.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream Topping
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the heavy cream to soft peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread over the top just before serving.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days — the milk soak means it must stay chilled.

steps: Preheat oven to 160°C (325°F). Melt the caramel sugar in a saucepan until deep amber, then pour into the bottom of a bundt pan and swirl to coat.
Blend condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream cheese, flan eggs, and vanilla until smooth — this is the flan batter.
Whisk flour, cocoa, cake sugar, baking powder, and baking soda together, then mix in oil, cake eggs, and milk until smooth — this is the cake batter.
Pour the cake batter over the caramel in the pan, then gently pour the flan batter on top without stirring — they'll swap places as they bake.
Cover tightly with foil and set the pan in a larger roasting pan filled with hot water halfway up the sides. Bake 60-70 minutes until set.
Cool completely, then chill at least 4 hours before inverting onto a plate.

filling.name: Flan Layer
filling.prep: Blend the condensed milk, evaporated milk, cream cheese, flan eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
filling.applicationNotes: Pour gently over the cake batter without stirring — the two layers swap places as they bake in a water bath.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill at least 4 hours before inverting so both layers hold their shape when unmolded.

frostingFinish.name: Caramel
frostingFinish.prep: Melt the sugar in a saucepan until deep amber.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour into the bottom of the bundt pan and swirl to coat before adding the batters — it becomes the glossy top once the cake is inverted.

equipment: Larger roasting pan for the water bath
storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch round pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla and almond extract.
Alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk until just combined. Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Simmer syrup sugar and water into a light syrup, then brush over each cooled layer.
Whisk egg whites and frosting sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff peaks. Beat in frosting butter a little at a time until smooth meringue buttercream forms.
Frost between layers and over the outside of the cake.

filling.name: Simple Syrup Soak
filling.prep: Simmer the syrup sugar and water into a light syrup.
filling.applicationNotes: Brush over each cooled cake layer before frosting.

frostingFinish.name: Meringue Buttercream
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk egg whites and sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff peaks. Beat in the butter a little at a time until a smooth buttercream forms.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Frost between the syrup-soaked layers and over the outside.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease an 8-inch springform pan.
Whisk melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla together.
Fold in flour, cocoa, and salt until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 20 minutes — the center should still be very soft and underbaked.
Cool slightly, dust with powdered sugar, and serve with whipped cream.

filling.note: A single dense, fudgy layer with no filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally finished with a dusting of powdered sugar and served alongside whipped cream, rather than a spread-on frosting.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 2-3 days — best eaten while still slightly gooey.

steps: Warm honey, sugar, and butter together in a saucepan until melted, then whisk in baking soda — it will foam up.
Remove from heat, whisk in eggs, then stir in flour until a soft dough forms. Divide into 8 portions and roll each thin.
Bake each layer at 175°C (350°F) for 4-5 minutes until golden; trim edges while warm and reserve the trimmings.
Whip sour cream, powdered sugar, and heavy cream together into a frosting.
Stack the layers with frosting between each, frost the outside, then press the reserved crumbs onto the sides.
Refrigerate at least 8 hours, ideally overnight, so the layers soften into a torte before serving.

filling.note: The sour cream frosting is spread between the layers as well as over the outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Sour Cream Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the sour cream, powdered sugar, and heavy cream together into a smooth frosting.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Stack the layers with frosting between each, frost the outside, then press the reserved baked crumbs onto the sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Refrigerate at least 8 hours, ideally overnight, so the layers soften into a torte before serving.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days — it improves as it sits.

steps: Mix flour, salt, yeast, and warm water into a smooth dough. Let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Roll out the dough and enclose the cold butter block, then fold and roll repeatedly as you would puff pastry, sprinkling sugar between folds and chilling between each to keep the butter firm.
After the final fold, roll out and cut into squares, fold the corners into the center, and place in a muffin tin, sprinkling more sugar on top.
Proof 45 minutes, then bake at 220°C (425°F) for 20-25 minutes until deeply caramelized and shattering-crisp on the outside.

filling.note: The sugar is folded directly into the laminated layers during lamination, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: The caramelized, shattering-crisp exterior comes from the sugar caramelizing during baking, not from an applied glaze.

storage: Best eaten the day it's baked; keeps at room temperature, loosely covered, for 1 day.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Melt the dark chocolate and butter together. Beat egg yolks with half the sugar until pale, then whisk into the chocolate mixture.
Whip egg whites with the remaining sugar to soft peaks, then fold into the batter along with the flour.
Bake 45-50 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs. Cool completely.
Slice the cake in half horizontally, spread warmed apricot jam between the layers and over the top and sides.
Warm the glaze cream, pour over the glaze chocolate and stir smooth, then pour over the cake, letting it drip down the sides. Let set before slicing.

filling.name: Apricot Jam
filling.prep: Warm the jam gently until spreadable.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread between the two sliced layers and over the top and sides as a thin coat before glazing.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Glaze
frostingFinish.prep: Warm the cream, pour over the chopped chocolate, and stir until smooth and glossy.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour over the jam-coated cake, letting it drip down the sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Let the glaze set at room temperature before slicing.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days — the glaze seals in moisture.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a loaf pan.
Cream butter, sugar, and mawa together until smooth, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Fold in flour, baking powder, cardamom, and nutmeg, alternating with milk.
Pour into the pan and bake 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

filling.note: A single loaf cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 165°C (325°F). Whisk flour, baking powder, and half the sugar together.
Whisk in egg yolks, coconut milk, oil, and pandan extract until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites with cream of tartar, gradually adding the remaining sugar, to stiff peaks.
Fold the egg whites into the batter in three additions, then pour into an ungreased tube pan.
Bake 45-50 minutes until springy to the touch. Invert the pan immediately and cool completely upside down before releasing.

filling.note: A single chiffon cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, unfrosted, to let the pandan flavor and airy texture speak for themselves.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 2-3 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Mix semolina, coconut, sugar, yogurt, melted butter, and baking powder into a thick batter.
Spread into the pan, score into diamonds, and press an almond into the center of each piece.
Bake 30-35 minutes until golden.
Simmer syrup sugar, water, lemon juice, and orange blossom water into a syrup, then pour the hot syrup over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven.

filling.note: A single-layer semolina cake, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Syrup Soak
frostingFinish.prep: Simmer the syrup sugar, water, lemon juice, and orange blossom water into a syrup.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour the hot syrup over the cake as soon as it comes out of the oven, letting it soak in fully.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days — the syrup keeps it moist.

steps: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F) and prepare a water bath. Melt cream cheese, butter, and milk together until smooth.
Whisk in egg yolks, flour, cornstarch, and lemon juice.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites with cream of tartar, gradually adding sugar, to soft peaks.
Fold the egg whites into the cheese mixture in three additions.
Pour into a lined pan, place in the water bath, and bake 65-70 minutes until golden and just set.
Turn off the oven and let the cake cool inside with the door ajar to prevent sinking.

filling.note: A single soufflé-style cheesecake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or topping, to showcase its jiggly texture.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days — best eaten within a day for peak jiggle.

steps: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F) and line a loaf pan with parchment extending above the rim.
Whisk eggs and sugar over a warm water bath until warm to the touch and doubled in volume.
Whisk in honey and milk, then fold in the bread flour in three additions.
Pour into the pan, tap firmly on the counter to release air bubbles, and bake 50-55 minutes.
Drop the pan from a small height as soon as it comes out of the oven to prevent shrinking, then cool wrapped in plastic to keep it moist.

filling.note: A single loaf cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or glaze.

panSize: Loaf pan, parchment-lined above the rim
storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped in plastic, for 2-3 days — the wrap keeps it moist.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9x13-inch pan.
Mix base flour, base sugar, base butter, base egg, and baking powder into a soft dough and press evenly into the pan.
Beat cream cheese and topping butter until smooth, add topping eggs and vanilla, then beat in powdered sugar until smooth.
Pour the topping over the base.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the edges are golden but the center still jiggles slightly — it should never fully set.
Cool completely before slicing; dust with powdered sugar.

filling.note: A single buttery base with a topping baked directly on top, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Topping
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese and topping butter until smooth, add the topping eggs and vanilla, then beat in the powdered sugar until smooth.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour over the pressed-in base before baking together; dust with powdered sugar once cooled.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch pans.
Whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder, and salt together.
Whisk in eggs, buttermilk, oil, and hot coffee until smooth — the batter will be thin.
Divide between pans and bake 22-25 minutes. Cool completely, then crumble one layer into fine crumbs for coating.

Whisk pudding sugar, pudding cocoa, and cornstarch in a saucepan, whisk in pudding milk and egg yolks, and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened into a pudding. Stir in pudding butter, then chill.
Stack the two remaining cake layers with pudding filling between them and on top, then press the reserved crumbs over the entire outside.

filling.name: Chocolate Pudding
filling.prep: Whisk the pudding sugar, pudding cocoa, and cornstarch in a saucepan, whisk in the pudding milk and egg yolks, and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir in the pudding butter, then chill.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread between the two remaining cake layers and over the top.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill the pudding fully before assembling so it holds its shape.

frostingFinish.note: Finished with crumbs from the crumbled third cake layer pressed over the outside, rather than a separate frosting.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — the pudding filling needs to stay chilled.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 9-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar, alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk, then fold in whipped egg whites and vanilla.
Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Cook filling egg yolks, filling sugar, and filling butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat and stir in bourbon, pecans, and cherries.
Spread the filling between the layers only, leaving the outside of the cake bare in the traditional style. Let set before slicing.

filling.name: Bourbon-Pecan-Cherry Filling
filling.prep: Cook the filling egg yolks, filling sugar, and filling butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened. Remove from heat and stir in the bourbon, pecans, and cherries.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread between the layers only.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left bare on the outside — only the filling shows between the layers.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking dish.
Beat sugar and egg until light, then mix in melted butter and apricot jam.
Whisk baking soda into vinegar — it will fizz — then add to the batter alternately with flour and milk.
Pour into the dish and bake 35-40 minutes until golden and set.
Warm sauce cream, sauce butter, and sauce sugar together until the butter melts, then pour the hot sauce evenly over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven, letting it soak in.

filling.note: A single baked pudding with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Hot Butter Sauce
frostingFinish.prep: Warm the sauce cream, sauce butter, and sauce sugar together until the butter melts.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour the hot sauce evenly over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven, letting it soak in completely.

storage: Keeps refrigerated, covered, for 3-4 days — best served warm.

steps: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F) and draw a 9-inch circle on parchment paper as a guide.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, then gradually add sugar and whip to stiff, glossy peaks.
Fold in cornstarch, vinegar, and vanilla, then mound onto the parchment within the circle, smoothing the sides and creating a slight well in the center.
Bake 60-75 minutes, then turn off the oven and let it cool completely inside with the door closed to prevent cracking.
Top with whipped cream and passionfruit (or other fresh fruit) just before serving.

filling.note: A single meringue base with no internal filling.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream & Passionfruit
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the cream to soft peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Top with whipped cream and passionfruit (or other fresh fruit) just before serving.

storage: Assemble just before serving — the meringue softens once topped.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a square pan. Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then alternate adding flour/baking powder with milk and vanilla.
Pour into the pan and bake 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely, then chill — it's easier to cut and dip when cold.
Cut the cooled sponge into squares.
Whisk icing sugar, icing cocoa, and icing milk into a thin chocolate icing.
Dip each square in the icing, letting excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.
Let set on a wire rack before serving.

filling.note: A plain sponge cut into squares, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Icing & Coconut
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the icing sugar, icing cocoa, and icing milk into a thin chocolate icing.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Dip each sponge square in the icing, letting excess drip off, then roll in desiccated coconut.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Let set on a wire rack before serving.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease three 8-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, cocoa, and baking powder alternately with milk.
Divide between pans and bake 22-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Drizzle each layer with kirsch, then whip the cream with sugar to soft peaks.
Stack layers with cherries and whipped cream between each, frost the outside, and cover with chocolate shavings and extra cherries.

filling.name: Cherry & Kirsch
filling.prep: Drizzle kirsch over each cake layer before assembling.
filling.applicationNotes: Scatter cherries over the whipped cream between each layer.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream & Chocolate Shavings
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the cream with sugar to soft peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Use the same whipped cream both between the layers (with the cherries) and to frost the outside; finish with chocolate shavings and extra cherries on top.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days — the whipped cream and cherries need to stay chilled.

steps: Warm the milk, dissolve the yeast in it, and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix flour, sugar, and salt in a large bowl, add the yeast mixture, eggs, egg yolks, and vanilla, then knead until smooth.
Knead in the butter a little at a time until fully incorporated, then fold in candied peel and raisins.
Place in a tall round mold and proof until doubled, about 3-4 hours.
Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 45-50 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean; cool upside down to keep its tall shape.

filling.note: The candied peel and raisins are kneaded directly into the dough, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left plain, with no icing or glaze.

equipment: Stand mixer or hands for kneading
storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for about a week.

steps: Roll the puff pastry into a log, slice into rounds, and press into a muffin tin to form cups.
Whisk sugar and cornstarch, then whisk in milk, cream, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel; simmer until slightly thickened.
Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel, then whisk the hot mixture into the egg yolks.
Fill the pastry cups with custard and bake at 245°C (475°F) for 15-18 minutes until deeply spotted and caramelized on top.
Cool slightly and dust with cinnamon before serving.

filling.name: Egg Custard
filling.prep: Whisk sugar and cornstarch, then whisk in milk, cream, cinnamon stick, and lemon peel; simmer until slightly thickened. Remove the cinnamon and lemon peel, then whisk the hot mixture into the egg yolks.
filling.applicationNotes: Fill the pastry cups with the custard before baking at very high heat until deeply spotted and caramelized on top.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally finished with a light dusting of ground cinnamon rather than a frosting.

storage: Best eaten the day they're baked; keeps refrigerated up to 2 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Cream butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, beat in eggs one at a time and vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder until just combined.
Divide between pans and bake 20-25 minutes until golden and springy. Cool completely.
Spread jam over one layer, top with whipped cream, sandwich with the second layer, and dust with powdered sugar.

filling.name: Jam & Whipped Cream
filling.prep: No cooking required — the jam is used as-is and the cream is whipped to soft peaks.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread jam over one layer, top with whipped cream, then sandwich with the second layer.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally finished with a simple dusting of powdered sugar rather than a frosting.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days — the whipped cream filling needs to stay chilled.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Warm the stout and butter together until melted, then whisk in cocoa and sugar.
Whisk in sour cream, eggs, and vanilla, then fold in flour and baking soda.
Pour into the pan and bake 45-50 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat cream cheese, powdered sugar, and cream together and spread over the cooled cake — traditionally left white like the head of a stout.

filling.note: A single-layer cake, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar, and cream together until smooth.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread over the top only, traditionally left white like the head of a stout.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 165°C (330°F). Mix crushed biscuits with melted butter and press into a 9-inch springform pan.
Beat cheese and sugar until smooth, then beat in eggs one at a time.
Mix in cornstarch, vanilla, and lemon zest until smooth.
Pour over the crust and bake 60-65 minutes until just set with a slight jiggle in the center.
Cool in the oven with the door ajar, then chill at least 4 hours before slicing.

filling.note: The cheese custard is the cake itself, poured directly over the crust rather than sandwiched as a separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or topping.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Whip eggs and sugar until thick and pale, then fold in flour and melted butter.
Spread thin layers of batter on parchment and bake 5-6 minutes each until golden; you'll need 6 layers total.
Beat buttercream butter, powdered sugar, and melted chocolate together into a smooth buttercream.
Stack five layers with buttercream between each and over the outside.
Melt the caramel sugar, pour over the sixth layer, quickly cut into wedges before it hardens, and arrange on top as a garnish.

filling.note: The chocolate buttercream is spread between the layers as well as over the outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Buttercream & Caramel Wedges
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the buttercream butter, powdered sugar, and melted chocolate together into a smooth buttercream. Separately, melt the caramel sugar until amber.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Stack five layers with buttercream between each and over the outside. Pour the caramel over the sixth layer, quickly cut into wedges before it hardens, and arrange on top as a garnish.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in yogurt and oil.
Fold in flour, semolina, baking powder, and coconut until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Meanwhile, simmer syrup sugar, water, and lemon juice into a syrup.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake as soon as it comes out of the oven and let it fully absorb before slicing.

filling.note: A single semolina cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Lemon Syrup Soak
frostingFinish.prep: Simmer the syrup sugar, water, and lemon juice into a syrup.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake as soon as it comes out of the oven and let it fully absorb before slicing.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days — the syrup keeps it moist.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in oil.
Fold in flour, ground walnuts, breadcrumbs, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Pour into the pan and bake 35-40 minutes until deep golden. Meanwhile, simmer syrup sugar, water, honey, and cinnamon stick into a syrup.
Pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and let it soak in fully before serving.

filling.note: A single walnut cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Spiced Honey Syrup
frostingFinish.prep: Simmer the syrup sugar, water, honey, and cinnamon stick into a syrup.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour the warm syrup over the hot cake and let it soak in fully before serving.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 5-6 days — the syrup keeps it moist.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Boil whole oranges (skin on) for 1.5 hours until very soft, then cool and purée in a food processor, removing seeds.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch springform pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, fold in the orange purée, then almond flour, baking powder, and cardamom.
Pour into the pan and bake 50-55 minutes until golden and set (this cake stays moist — a toothpick may come out slightly damp).
Cool completely in the pan before releasing, as it's delicate while warm.

filling.note: A single flourless cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or glaze.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — it stays moist thanks to the orange purée.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch round pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in yogurt, oil, and rose water.
Fold in almond flour, semolina, baking powder, and cardamom.
Pour into the pan and bake 35-40 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool, then scatter chopped pistachios and dried rose petals (if available) over the top before serving.

filling.note: A single cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Pistachio Topping
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Scatter over the cooled cake along with dried rose petals, if available, before serving.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Mix golden syrup, oil, and lye water together, then work in flour to form a smooth dough. Rest 1 hour.
Divide lotus seed paste into portions and wrap each around a salted egg yolk.
Divide the dough into smaller portions, flatten, and wrap around each lotus paste ball, sealing completely.
Press each into a mooncake mold to shape, then place on a lined baking sheet.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 5 minutes, cool slightly, brush with egg wash, then bake another 15 minutes until golden.

filling.name: Lotus Paste & Salted Egg Yolk
filling.prep: Divide the lotus seed paste into portions and wrap each around a salted egg yolk.
filling.applicationNotes: Wrap the dough completely around each lotus-paste ball, sealing fully before pressing into the mold.

frostingFinish.name: Egg Wash
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the egg yolk and water together.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Brush over the shaped mooncakes partway through baking for a glossy finish.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for about a week — flavor improves after 1-2 days as the crust softens.

steps: Preheat oven to 165°C (330°F) and line an 8-inch round pan.
Whip eggs and sugar until thick and pale (ribbon stage), then gently fold in flour.
Fold in milk, oil, and vanilla, then pour into the pan and bake 25-28 minutes. Cool completely.
Whip cream and sugar to stiff peaks. Slice the sponge into three layers.
Stack layers with whipped cream and sliced strawberries between each, then frost the outside smooth and decorate with whole strawberries.

filling.note: The whipped cream and strawberries are used both between the layers and over the outside, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream & Strawberries
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the cream and sugar to stiff peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Stack the sliced layers with whipped cream and sliced strawberries between each, then frost the outside smooth and decorate with whole strawberries.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days — fresh strawberries mean it doesn't keep as long as most layer cakes.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Whisk eggs and sugar, then whisk in oil, coconut milk, ube halaya, and ube extract.
Fold in flour and baking powder until just combined.
Divide between pans and bake 28-32 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat frosting butter, powdered sugar, and ube halaya together and frost between layers and over the outside.

filling.note: The ube buttercream is spread between the layers as well as over the outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Ube Buttercream
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the frosting butter, powdered sugar, and ube halaya together until smooth and evenly colored.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Frost between the layers and over the outside.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Dissolve yeast in a little warm water with a pinch of sugar; let it foam for 10 minutes.
Whisk tapioca starch, rice flour, remaining sugar, and salt together, then whisk in coconut milk, eggs, and pandan extract.
Stir in the yeast mixture and let the batter rest 2 hours until bubbly.
Pour into a greased pan and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 30-35 minutes until deep golden with a honeycomb of holes inside.
Cool before slicing — the texture should be chewy and springy.

filling.note: A single honeycomb-textured cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or topping.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 2-3 days.

steps: Whisk all dry ingredients together, then whisk in coconut milk and salt until smooth. Divide the batter in half and tint one half with pandan juice.
Grease a square pan and steam for 5 minutes to warm it, then pour a thin layer of plain batter and steam 3-4 minutes until set.
Pour a thin layer of the green batter on top and steam another 3-4 minutes; repeat, alternating layers, until the batter is used (traditionally 9 layers).
Steam the final layer for 10 minutes to fully set.
Cool completely before slicing into diamonds — the layers should peel apart slightly when eaten.

filling.note: The alternating pandan and plain layers are steamed directly on top of one another from the same batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or topping.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days — the layers hold together best chilled.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) with the broiler available, and grease an 8-inch square pan.
Cream butter and sugar until very light, then beat in condensed milk.
Whisk egg yolks separately until thick, then fold into the butter mixture along with flour and mixed spice.
Pour a very thin layer of batter into the pan and broil 2-3 minutes until golden; repeat, adding thin layers and broiling each, until the batter is used (15-20 layers).
Cool completely before slicing thin — the finished cake should show dozens of fine spiced layers.

filling.note: The cake is built entirely from dozens of thin broiled layers of its own batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing, to show off the fine layered cross-section.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 1-2 weeks — it's traditionally made ahead.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease two 8-inch pans.
Whisk flour, cocoa, sugar, and baking powder together, then whisk in eggs, milk, and oil.
Divide between pans and bake 25-28 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Cook condensed milk, frosting cocoa, and frosting butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat a spoon, about 10 minutes; cool slightly.
Spread the brigadeiro frosting between layers and over the outside, then cover generously with chocolate sprinkles.

filling.note: The brigadeiro frosting is spread between the layers as well as over the outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Brigadeiro Frosting & Sprinkles
frostingFinish.prep: Cook the condensed milk, frosting cocoa, and frosting butter over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick enough to coat a spoon, about 10 minutes. Cool slightly before spreading.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread between the layers and over the outside, then cover generously with chocolate sprinkles.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Melt base butter, sugar, and cocoa together, whisk in the egg, and cook gently until thickened. Stir in graham crumbs, coconut, and walnuts, then press into a lined 9-inch square pan and chill.
Beat filling butter, custard powder, filling sugar, and filling milk together until smooth and spreadable.
Spread the filling over the chilled base and chill again until firm.
Melt the topping chocolate and butter together, then pour over the filling layer, tilting to cover evenly.
Chill until the chocolate sets, then cut into small bars.

filling.name: Custard Filling
filling.prep: Beat the filling butter, custard powder, filling sugar, and filling milk together until smooth and spreadable.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread over the chilled crumb base.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill again until firm before adding the chocolate topping.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Topping
frostingFinish.prep: Melt the topping chocolate and butter together.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pour over the set custard layer, tilting to cover evenly.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill until the chocolate sets before cutting into bars.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 weeks — best kept cold since it never gets baked.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Combine flour, butter, egg yolks, and baking powder into a smooth dough.
Divide into 6-8 portions, roll each paper-thin, and bake 6-8 minutes each until golden and crisp.
Stack the baked wafer layers with dulce de leche spread between each.
Whip egg whites and meringue sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff, glossy peaks.
Pile the meringue over the top and sides, and lightly torch or broil until golden in spots.

filling.name: Dulce de Leche
filling.prep: No cooking required — the dulce de leche is used as-is.
filling.applicationNotes: Stack the baked wafer layers with dulce de leche spread between each.

frostingFinish.name: Torched Meringue
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the egg whites and meringue sugar over a double boiler until warm, then whip to stiff, glossy peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Pile over the top and sides, then lightly torch or broil until golden in spots.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Bake each puff pastry sheet between two baking sheets (to keep it flat) for 15-18 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cool the pastry sheets completely, then trim to even rectangles.
Stack the sheets with a generous layer of dulce de leche spread between each.
Dust the top layer heavily with powdered sugar.
Chill at least 1 hour before slicing so the layers hold together cleanly.

filling.name: Dulce de Leche
filling.prep: No cooking required — the dulce de leche is used as-is.
filling.applicationNotes: Stack the cooled, trimmed pastry sheets with a generous layer of dulce de leche between each.

frostingFinish.name: Powdered Sugar Dusting
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Dust the top layer heavily just before serving.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days — best eaten within a day for the crispest layers.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch square pan.
Cream base butter and base sugar, beat in the egg yolk, then fold in flour and baking powder to form a soft dough. Press into the pan.
Spread raspberry jam evenly over the base.
Whip egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add meringue sugar and whip to stiff peaks, then fold in coconut.
Spread the coconut meringue over the jam layer and bake 30-35 minutes until golden. Cool completely before slicing.

filling.name: Raspberry Jam
filling.prep: No cooking required — the jam is used as-is.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread evenly over the pressed-in shortbread base.

frostingFinish.name: Coconut Meringue
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add the meringue sugar and whip to stiff peaks, then fold in the coconut.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread over the jam layer and bake together until golden.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days.

substitutions.replacement: not recommended — this recipe relies on almond flour

steps: Mix almond flour and powdered sugar, then work in egg whites to form a smooth, firm dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Roll the dough into ropes and shape into graduated rings using ring molds (18 rings from largest to smallest).
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden; cool completely on the molds.
Whisk the icing egg white, icing sugar, and lemon juice into a stiff royal icing.
Stack the rings from largest to smallest into a tower, piping icing in zigzags between each layer to secure and decorate.

filling.note: A tower of stacked almond rings with no internal filling.

frostingFinish.name: Royal Icing
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the icing egg white, icing sugar, and lemon juice into a stiff royal icing.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Stack the cooled rings from largest to smallest into a tower, piping icing in zigzags between each layer to secure and decorate.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, uncovered, for about a week — it's meant to dry slightly and firm up.

substitutions.replacement: omit, increase flour by the same amount

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease small cylindrical molds (or a muffin tin).
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, rum, and almond extract.
Fold in flour, almond flour, breadcrumbs, and baking powder.
Divide into the molds and bake 20-25 minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Top each cake with a small dollop of raspberry jam surrounded by a thin ring of powdered sugar icing.

filling.note: Small individual cakes with no internal filling.

frostingFinish.name: Raspberry Jam & Icing Ring
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the icing sugar and water into a thin icing.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Top each cooled cake with a small dollop of raspberry jam surrounded by a thin ring of icing.

panSize: Small cylindrical molds or muffin tin
storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Bring water and butter to a boil, add flour all at once and stir until a smooth dough forms.
Off heat, beat in eggs one at a time until glossy. Pipe into a ring on a baking sheet, top with almonds, and bake 30-35 minutes until deeply golden. Cool completely.
Make pastry cream: whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, then temper in hot milk. Cook until thickened, then whisk in praline paste. Chill fully.
Split the choux ring horizontally. Pipe the praline cream generously into the bottom half.
Replace the top half and dust with powdered sugar before serving.

filling.name: Praline Pastry Cream
filling.prep: Whisk the egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, then temper with hot milk. Cook until thickened, then whisk in the praline paste. Chill fully.
filling.applicationNotes: Split the choux ring horizontally and pipe the cream generously into the bottom half.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill the pastry cream completely before piping so it holds its shape.

frostingFinish.name: Powdered Sugar Dusting
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Dust over the top just before serving.

storage: Refrigerate, assembled, up to 1 day — choux softens quickly once filled.

steps: Beat ricotta with powdered sugar until smooth, then fold in candied fruit, chocolate chips, and lemon zest.
Line a bowl or cassata mold with thin sponge slices.
Fill with the ricotta mixture and top with more sponge. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Unmold and wrap the sides in rolled-out green marzipan.
Top with white icing and decorate with additional candied fruit.

filling.name: Sweet Ricotta
filling.prep: Beat the ricotta with powdered sugar until smooth, then fold in the candied fruit, chocolate chips, and lemon zest.
filling.applicationNotes: Fill the sponge-lined mold with the ricotta mixture and top with more sponge.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill for at least 4 hours so the filling sets before unmolding.

frostingFinish.name: Marzipan & Icing
frostingFinish.prep: Roll the marzipan out to wrap the sides.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Wrap the unmolded cassata in marzipan, then top with white icing and decorate with additional candied fruit.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days — the ricotta filling needs to stay chilled.

steps: Preheat the broiler. Cream butter and sugar, beat in egg yolks and vanilla, then fold in flour and cornstarch.
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks and fold into the batter.
Spread a very thin layer of batter over the base of a greased round pan and broil until just set and golden, about 2-3 minutes.
Spread another thin layer directly over the first and broil again. Repeat 10-15 times, building visible layers.
Cool completely, brush with warm apricot jam, and finish with a chocolate glaze if desired before slicing.

filling.note: No separate filling is used — each thin layer is broiled directly onto the previous one, building the cake from the batter itself.

frostingFinish.name: Apricot & Chocolate Glaze
frostingFinish.prep: Warm the apricot jam until spreadable; melt the chocolate if using.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Brush the cooled cake with warm apricot jam, then finish with a chocolate glaze if desired.

panSize: Round pan (built up in thin broiled layers)
storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days thanks to the glaze seal.

steps: Combine ground hazelnuts, flour, sugar, cinnamon, and cloves. Cut in cold butter until crumbly.
Work in egg yolks and lemon zest until a firm dough forms. Chill 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Press two-thirds of the dough into a tart pan and spread with redcurrant jam.
Roll the remaining dough into strips and arrange in a lattice over the jam.
Bake 35-40 minutes until the lattice is golden. Cool completely before slicing.

filling.name: Redcurrant Jam
filling.prep: No cooking required — the jam is used as-is.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread over the pressed-in dough before topping with the lattice.

frostingFinish.note: Finished simply with its own pastry lattice on top rather than a separate frosting or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days — traditionally made a day ahead.

steps: Soak raisins and candied fruit in port wine for at least 30 minutes.
Proof yeast in warm milk with a pinch of sugar. Mix into flour, sugar, eggs, and butter to form a soft dough.
Knead in the soaked fruit. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1.5 hours.
Shape into a ring on a baking sheet, cover, and let rise again 45 minutes.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 30-35 minutes until deeply golden. Brush with warm jam or egg wash to finish.

filling.note: The port-soaked fruit is kneaded directly into the dough, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally brushed with warm jam or egg wash for shine, but this data does not track a separate finish ingredient beyond what's already in the dough.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 4-5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a round cake pan.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick.
Fold in almond flour, lemon zest, and cinnamon until just combined.
Pour into the pan and bake 35-40 minutes until golden and set. Cool completely.
Lay a Cross of Saint James stencil over the top and dust generously with powdered sugar, then lift the stencil away.

filling.note: A single-layer almond cake, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Powdered Sugar Stencil
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Lay a Cross of Saint James stencil over the top and dust generously with powdered sugar, then lift the stencil away.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, and almond extract.
Divide the batter in half and tint one half pink. Bake each in a separate loaf pan section 25-30 minutes. Cool completely.
Trim and cut each sponge into two long strips of equal size.
Brush strips with warm apricot jam and assemble into a checkerboard pattern, gluing with more jam.
Wrap the whole assembled cake in a sheet of rolled marzipan, trimming the seam neatly.

filling.name: Apricot Jam
filling.prep: Warm the jam until spreadable.
filling.applicationNotes: Brush over the trimmed sponge strips and use it to glue them into the checkerboard pattern.

frostingFinish.name: Marzipan Wrap
frostingFinish.prep: Roll the marzipan out into a sheet large enough to wrap the assembled cake.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Wrap the checkerboard cake in the marzipan sheet, trimming the seam neatly.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F) and line a deep round cake pan.
Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs one at a time, then fold in flour, baking powder, orange zest, and whisky.
Fold in the dried fruit until evenly distributed.
Spread into the pan and arrange whole almonds in concentric circles over the top.
Bake 1.5-2 hours until a skewer comes out clean, covering loosely with foil if it browns too quickly.

filling.note: A single fruitcake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Finished with a ring of whole almonds pressed onto the top before baking, rather than a separate icing — traditional Dundee cake is never iced.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 2-3 weeks — it improves with age like most fruitcakes.

steps: Rub cold butter into flour, baking powder, and nutmeg until it resembles breadcrumbs.
Stir in sugar and currants, then bind with egg and milk into a soft dough.
Roll out to about 1cm thick and cut into rounds.
Cook on a lightly greased griddle or heavy skillet over medium heat, 3 minutes per side until golden.
Dust with a little extra sugar while still warm.

filling.note: Individual griddle cakes with no filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally finished with just a dusting of the dough's own sugar while warm, rather than a separate icing.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder. Pour into a greased pan and bake 25-30 minutes until just set.
Meanwhile, melt topping butter with brown sugar and coconut into a spreadable paste.
Spread the coconut topping evenly over the warm cake.
Return to the oven under the broiler for 2-3 minutes until the topping is bubbling and caramelized. Cool before slicing.

filling.note: A single sponge cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Coconut Caramel Topping
frostingFinish.prep: Melt the topping butter with the brown sugar and coconut into a spreadable paste.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread over the warm cake, then broil for 2-3 minutes until bubbling and caramelized.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a baking dish.
Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, then whisk in melted butter, milk, and vanilla.
Fold in flour and baking powder to make a thick batter.
Pour into the dish and scatter cherries evenly over the top — they will sink slightly as it bakes.
Bake 35-40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Dust with powdered sugar to serve.

filling.note: The cherries are scattered directly over the poured batter and sink in as it bakes, rather than being layered in as a separate filling.

frostingFinish.name: Powdered Sugar Dusting
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Dust over the cooled cake before serving.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 2-3 days — best eaten fresh while the cherries are juicy.

steps: Proof yeast in warm milk with a spoonful of sugar. Mix into flour, remaining sugar, eggs, and orange zest to form a soft dough. Knead in butter gradually.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1.5-2 hours.
Mix ground walnuts, cocoa powder, and rum into a spreadable filling.
Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread with filling, and roll up tightly. Place in a loaf pan, cover, and let rise 45 minutes.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 40-45 minutes, tenting with foil if it browns too fast.

filling.name: Walnut-Cocoa Filling
filling.prep: Mix the ground walnuts, cocoa powder, and rum into a spreadable filling.
filling.applicationNotes: Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread with the filling, and roll up tightly before placing in the loaf pan.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left plain, with no icing or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 4-5 days.

steps: Whip egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add sugar, and whip to a stiff, glossy meringue. Fold in flour and hazelnuts.
Spread into two thin rounds on parchment and bake at 150°C (300°F) for about 1 hour until dry and crisp. Cool completely.
Beat butter until fluffy, then gradually beat in condensed milk and vanilla until smooth.
Spread buttercream between the two meringue layers and over the top and sides.
Chill for at least 6 hours (overnight is best) so the meringue softens slightly before slicing.

filling.note: The condensed-milk buttercream is spread between the meringue layers as well as over the top and sides, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Condensed Milk Buttercream
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the butter until fluffy, then gradually beat in the condensed milk and vanilla until smooth.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread between the two meringue layers and over the top and sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, so the meringue softens slightly before slicing.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days.

steps: Whip egg whites to stiff peaks, gradually adding sugar. Fold in ground walnuts and flour.
Divide between two or three thin round pans and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 20-25 minutes. Cool completely.
Melt chocolate with cream and cool slightly. Beat butter with powdered sugar, then beat in the cooled chocolate mixture.
Spread chocolate cream between the layers and over the top and sides.
Chill at least 3 hours before slicing to let the cream set.

filling.note: The chocolate cream is spread between the layers as well as over the top and sides, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Chocolate Cream
frostingFinish.prep: Melt the chocolate with the cream and cool slightly. Beat the butter with powdered sugar, then beat in the cooled chocolate mixture.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Spread between the layers and over the top and sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill at least 3 hours before slicing to let the cream set.

panSize: Two or three thin round pans
storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days.

steps: Cut butter into flour until pea-sized, then bind with ice water and vinegar into a rough dough. Chill 30 minutes.
Divide into 8-10 portions, roll each paper-thin, and bake individually at 200°C (400°F) for 8-10 minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Make the custard: whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, temper with hot milk, then cook until thick. Stir in vanilla and cool completely.
Layer the pastry sheets with custard between each, ending with pastry on top.
Chill overnight so the layers soften slightly before slicing, and crush trimmings over the top to finish.

filling.name: Pastry Cream
filling.prep: Whisk egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch together, temper with hot milk, then cook until thick. Stir in vanilla and cool completely before using.
filling.textureGoal: Thick enough to hold its shape between the pastry sheets without oozing out.
filling.applicationNotes: Layer between each pastry sheet, ending with pastry on top.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill the assembled torte overnight so the layers soften slightly before slicing.

frostingFinish.note: Finished with crushed pastry trimmings scattered on top rather than a frosting.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days — the pastry cream filling needs to stay chilled.

steps: Whisk eggs and sugar until pale and thick, fold in flour and baking powder, and bake in a round pan at 175°C (350°F) for 25 minutes. Cool and slice into 3 layers.
Make pastry cream: whisk egg yolks, sugar, temper with hot milk, cook until thick, then cool completely.
Assemble: bottom sponge layer with raspberry jam, middle layer with pastry cream, top layer mounded with whipped cream into a dome shape.
Chill the domed cake until firm, then drape with a large circle of rolled marzipan, smoothing down the sides.
Trim the base neatly and finish with a small pink marzipan rose on top.

filling.name: Jam & Pastry Cream
filling.prep: Whisk the egg yolks and sugar, temper with hot milk, and cook until thick. Cool completely before assembling.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread jam over the bottom sponge layer, then spread pastry cream over the middle layer.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream Dome & Marzipan
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the cream to stiff peaks. Roll the marzipan into a large circle.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Mound the whipped cream over the top layer into a dome shape, chill until firm, then drape the marzipan over the dome, smoothing down the sides and trimming the base. Finish with a small marzipan rose on top.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill the domed cake until firm before draping with marzipan.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days.

steps: Whip egg whites to soft peaks, gradually add sugar, and whip to a stiff, glossy meringue.
Pipe or spread into small disks and bake at 100°C (210°F) for about 1.5 hours until fully dry. Cool completely.
Whip cream with powdered sugar to stiff peaks.
Sandwich two meringue disks together with whipped cream, then coat the entire outside generously in more whipped cream.
Roll the whole cream-coated cake in dark chocolate shavings until fully covered.

filling.note: The whipped cream is used both to sandwich the meringue disks and to coat the entire outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream & Chocolate Shavings
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the cream with powdered sugar to stiff peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Sandwich two meringue disks together with whipped cream, coat the entire outside generously in more whipped cream, then roll in dark chocolate shavings until fully covered.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 1 day — best eaten fresh before the meringue softens.

steps: Rub cold butter into flour and sugar, bind with egg into a dough, and chill 30 minutes.
Toss sliced apples with cinnamon, raisins, and lemon juice.
Press two-thirds of the dough into a tall springform pan, going up the sides. Sprinkle the base with breadcrumbs.
Fill with the apple mixture, mounding it high, and top with a lattice or crumbled cap of the remaining dough.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 60-70 minutes until deeply golden. Cool before unmolding.

filling.name: Spiced Apple Filling
filling.prep: Toss the sliced apples with cinnamon, raisins, and lemon juice.
filling.applicationNotes: Mound high into the pastry-lined pan before topping with a lattice or crumbled cap of the remaining dough.

frostingFinish.note: Finished with its own lattice pastry top rather than a separate frosting or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3-4 days.

steps: Whisk eggs and sugar until thick and pale, fold in ground almonds and flour, and bake two thin rounds at 175°C (350°F) for 20 minutes. Cool completely.
Bake a third thin round of crisp meringue (whip 2 extra egg whites with sugar) to use as the base layer for crunch.
Mix sugar syrup with half the kirsch. Beat butter with powdered sugar and the remaining kirsch for the buttercream.
Brush the sponge layers generously with the kirsch syrup. Layer meringue, then sponge and buttercream, alternating, finishing with buttercream on top and sides.
Press sliced almonds onto the sides and chill at least 2 hours before slicing.

filling.name: Kirsch Syrup Soak
filling.prep: Mix the sugar syrup with half the kirsch.
filling.applicationNotes: Brush generously over the sponge layers before stacking with the meringue crunch layer and buttercream.

frostingFinish.name: Kirsch Buttercream
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the butter with powdered sugar and the remaining kirsch.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Alternate meringue, sponge, and buttercream layers, finishing with buttercream on top and sides, then press sliced almonds onto the sides.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill at least 2 hours before slicing.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). Whisk eggs and sugar until very pale and tripled in volume, then fold in flour and melted butter.
Spread the batter in a very thin, even layer on a lined baking sheet and bake 6-8 minutes until just set — do not brown.
While still warm, spread the sponge evenly with softened guava paste.
Starting from one short edge, roll the sponge tightly into a spiral using the parchment paper to guide it.
Wrap tightly and chill at least 1 hour before slicing into thin spirals.

filling.name: Guava Paste
filling.prep: Soften the guava paste so it spreads easily.
filling.applicationNotes: Spread evenly over the warm thin sponge, then roll tightly from one short edge into a spiral.
filling.chillGuidance: Wrap tightly and chill at least 1 hour before slicing into thin spirals.

frostingFinish.note: Finished simply by the rolled spiral itself, with no icing or glaze.

storage: Refrigerate, wrapped, up to 5 days.

steps: Proof yeast in warm milk with a spoonful of sugar. Mix into flour, remaining sugar, eggs, and vanilla, then knead in softened butter gradually.
Knead in raisins and candied fruit until evenly distributed.
Cover and let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.
Shape into a tall round loaf, place in a paper panettone mold, and let rise again 1 hour.
Bake at 175°C (350°F) for 40-45 minutes, tenting with foil if it browns too quickly. Cool upside down if possible to keep its tall shape.

filling.note: The candied fruit and raisins are kneaded directly into the dough, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left plain, with no icing or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for about a week.

steps: Whisk eggs and sugar until pale, fold in flour and baking powder, and bake in a round pan at 175°C (350°F) for 20-25 minutes. Cool and slice into layers.
Whip egg whites with sugar over a double boiler until stiff and glossy, then continue whipping off heat until cooled — this is the meringue.
Crumble a portion of the sponge into small pieces for texture.
Assemble in a bowl or tall glass: sponge, dulce de leche, peaches, whipped cream, meringue, crumbled sponge — repeat the layers.
Finish with a final layer of whipped cream and meringue on top, and chill before serving.

filling.name: Dulce de Leche & Peaches
filling.prep: No cooking required beyond slicing the peaches — the dulce de leche is used as-is.
filling.applicationNotes: Layer with the sponge in a bowl or tall glass, alternating sponge, dulce de leche, and peaches.

frostingFinish.name: Whipped Cream & Meringue
frostingFinish.prep: Whip the egg whites with sugar over a double boiler until stiff and glossy, then continue whipping off heat until cooled. Whip the cream separately to soft peaks.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Layer whipped cream and meringue between the sponge layers along with the filling, then finish with a final layer of both on top.

panSize: Round pan, then assembled in a bowl or glass
storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 2 days.

ingredients.name: Mixed dried fruit, soaked in rum

steps: Soak dried fruit in rum for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Cream butter and brown sugar, beat in eggs and molasses, then fold in flour, baking powder, and cinnamon.
Fold in the soaked fruit along with any remaining rum.
Pour into a lined round pan and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 60-70 minutes, tenting with foil if it browns too fast.
Cool completely in the pan before turning out — the cake firms up and deepens in flavor as it sits.

filling.note: The rum-soaked dried fruit is folded directly into the batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left unfrosted — the cake firms up and deepens in flavor as it sits rather than being iced.

storage: Wrapped tightly, keeps for 1-2 weeks at room temperature and improves with age.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, and milk to make a smooth batter.
Divide between two round pans and bake 25-30 minutes. Cool completely.
Warm the guava paste slightly until spreadable and layer it between the two cake rounds.
Beat cream cheese with powdered sugar until smooth for the frosting.
Frost the top and sides, and finish with a few small cubes of guava paste on top.

filling.name: Guava Paste
filling.prep: Warm the guava paste slightly until spreadable.
filling.applicationNotes: Layer between the two cake rounds.

frostingFinish.name: Cream Cheese Frosting
frostingFinish.prep: Beat the cream cheese with powdered sugar until smooth.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Frost the top and sides, and finish with a few small cubes of guava paste on top.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 4 days.

steps: Soak dried fruit in rum and red wine for at least 1 week (up to several months) in a sealed jar, stirring occasionally.
Blend the soaked fruit into a coarse paste. Cream butter and brown sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, and mixed spice.
Fold in the fruit paste and burnt sugar browning for color and depth.
Pour into a lined round pan and bake at 150°C (300°F) for about 2 hours, tenting with foil once deeply browned.
Cool completely and, if desired, feed with a little more rum every few days before serving.

filling.note: The soaked fruit is blended into a paste and folded directly into the batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left unfrosted — sometimes 'fed' with a little more rum after baking, but never iced.

storage: Wrapped tightly, keeps for weeks at room temperature and improves with age — often 'fed' with rum every few days.

steps: Preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). Cream butter and sugar, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, and mixed spice.
Fold in the dried fruit. Spread half the batter into a lined round pan.
Lay a thin marzipan disk over the batter, then top with the remaining batter.
Bake 1.5-2 hours until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely.
Top with another marzipan disk and eleven marzipan balls arranged around the edge, then lightly toast the top under the broiler.

filling.note: A thin disk of marzipan is pressed inside as a hidden layer, using part of the marzipan listed under Frosting & Finish below.

frostingFinish.name: Marzipan
frostingFinish.prep: Divide the marzipan and roll into a thin disk for the hidden inner layer, plus a top disk and eleven marzipan balls (traditionally one for each of the eleven faithful apostles).
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Press one disk into the batter partway through filling the pan before baking. After baking, top with the second disk and the eleven balls, then lightly toast under the broiler.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for 2-3 weeks.

steps: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F) and grease a square baking pan.
Whisk together semolina, flour, sugar, turmeric, anise, and baking powder.
Stir in oil and milk until just combined into a thick batter.
Pour into the pan, scatter pine nuts over the top, and bake 30-35 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean.
Cool completely and cut into diamond-shaped pieces to serve.

filling.note: A single turmeric-spiced cake with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Finished with pine nuts pressed onto the top before baking, rather than a separate icing or glaze.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 4-5 days.

steps: Whisk eggs and brown sugar until well combined, then whisk in evaporated milk and oil.
Fold in flour and baking powder until just combined. Let the batter rest 20 minutes.
Pour into a greased heatproof cake pan that fits inside a steamer.
Steam over vigorously boiling water for 25-30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean, keeping the lid vented slightly to stop condensation dripping onto the cake.
Cool slightly before turning out and slicing into wedges.

filling.note: A single steamed sponge with no layers, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing or topping.

panSize: Heatproof pan that fits inside a steamer
storage: Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 2-3 days.

ingredients.name: Mixed dried fruit, soaked in rum

steps: Soak dried fruit in rum for at least 1 week, ideally longer, in a sealed jar.
Melt sugar in a dry pan until deep amber to make caramelized sugar syrup, then carefully add a splash of hot water to loosen it. Cool.
Cream butter with the caramel syrup, beat in eggs, then fold in flour, baking powder, and mixed spice.
Fold in the soaked fruit and any remaining liquid.
Bake at 150°C (300°F) for 1.5-2 hours in a lined pan, tenting with foil once deeply browned, until a skewer comes out clean.

filling.note: The rum-soaked dried fruit is folded directly into the batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally left unfrosted, relying on the caramel and rum for flavor rather than an applied finish.

storage: Wrapped tightly, keeps for 2-3 weeks at room temperature and improves with age.

steps: Cream butter, condensed milk, and sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in egg yolks gradually.
Fold in flour and mixed spice to make a thick, smooth batter. Divide into several portions and tint each a different color.
Spread a thin layer of one color into a greased pan and bake or broil briefly until just set.
Add the next colored layer directly on top and repeat, building up 10-15 thin layers in a deliberate pattern.
Cool completely before slicing to reveal the layered pattern inside.

filling.note: The cake is built entirely from many thin broiled layers of its own colored batter, so there is no separate filling.

frostingFinish.note: Traditionally served plain, with no icing, to show off the layered pattern inside.

storage: Keeps at room temperature, wrapped, for about a week — it's traditionally made ahead.

steps: Rub cold butter into flour to form a shortcrust dough, press into a tart pan, and blind-bake at 190°C (375°F) for 12 minutes.
Heat milk with sugar until just simmering. Whisk cornstarch and eggs together, then temper with the hot milk.
Return to the pan and cook, stirring, until thick and custard-like.
Pour into the baked crust and dust generously with cinnamon.
Chill at least 2 hours until fully set before slicing.

filling.name: Milk Custard
filling.prep: Heat the milk with sugar until just simmering. Whisk the cornstarch and eggs together, then temper with the hot milk. Return to the pan and cook, stirring, until thick and custard-like.
filling.applicationNotes: Pour into the blind-baked crust while still warm.
filling.chillGuidance: Chill at least 2 hours until fully set before slicing.

frostingFinish.name: Cinnamon Dusting
frostingFinish.prep: No preparation needed.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Dust generously over the custard while it is still warm, before chilling.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 3 days.

steps: Make a sugar syrup by boiling sugar, ginger, and water together, then chill it completely (ideally overnight).
Rub butter into flour and baking powder, then bind with milk into a soft dough. Roll out and cut into small rectangles.
Cut three slits into each rectangle and plait into a loose twist.
Deep-fry in hot oil until golden, about 2-3 minutes.
Immediately plunge the hot fried dough into the ice-cold syrup for a few seconds, then drain.

filling.note: A twisted fried dough with no internal filling.

frostingFinish.name: Ginger Syrup Soak
frostingFinish.prep: Boil the sugar, ginger, and water together into a syrup, then chill completely — ideally overnight, so it is ice-cold when the hot dough hits it.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Plunge the hot fried dough into the ice-cold syrup for a few seconds immediately after frying, then drain.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: The syrup must be fully chilled before use — the hot-to-cold contrast is what gives koeksisters their crisp shell and syrupy center.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 1 week — they hold their syrupy texture well chilled.

steps: Mix mashed sweet potato with flour, coconut, sugar, and cardamom into a firm dough.
Shape into small flattened rounds and press a little extra coconut filling into the center of each.
Heat oil to medium and deep-fry the rounds in batches until golden brown on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.

filling.note: A portion of the same sweet potato dough is pressed into the center of each round as a denser core, rather than a separately tracked filling.

frostingFinish.note: Deep-fried and served warm with no applied icing or glaze.

storage: Best eaten warm the day they're fried.

steps: Whip egg whites with sugar to stiff peaks, then fold in ground cashews. Spread into thin rounds and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 20-25 minutes until crisp. Cool completely.
Whisk egg yolks and condensed milk over a double boiler until thick, then cool and beat into softened butter to make the buttercream.
Layer the cashew meringue rounds with buttercream between each.
Coat the top and sides with more buttercream and press chopped cashews over the whole exterior.
Chill at least 4 hours before slicing — it cuts best cold.

filling.note: The cashew buttercream is spread between the meringue layers as well as over the outside, so no separate filling is used.

frostingFinish.name: Cashew Buttercream & Cashew Coating
frostingFinish.prep: Whisk the egg yolks and condensed milk over a double boiler until thick, then cool and beat into the softened butter.
frostingFinish.applicationNotes: Layer the cashew meringue rounds with buttercream between each, coat the top and sides with more buttercream, then press chopped cashews over the whole exterior.
frostingFinish.chillGuidance: Chill at least 4 hours before slicing — it cuts best cold.

storage: Refrigerate, covered, up to 5 days.

steps: Whisk rice flour, tapioca flour, sugar, and coconut milk into a smooth batter. Divide into portions and tint each a different color (leave one pandan-green).
